questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code ensures a commit is built only once at a time? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In execute(), the finally block calls activeBuilds.remove(run.commitSha(), run) rather than remove(run.commitSha()). What does the two-argument form accomplish?
choices: It removes all entries whose value equals this run
It removes the entry in a way that is atomic with respect to executor shutdown
It throws if the entry is missing, surfacing double-completion bugs
It removes the entry only if it is still mapped to this exact BuildRun, so it cannot evict a different run stored under the same commit

questions.prompt: When the executor has been shut down and submit() throws RejectedExecutionException inside trigger(), what is the resulting state?
choices: The run stays in activeBuilds as QUEUED, so later triggers for that commit return a build that never runs
The run is removed from activeBuilds and the exception propagates to the caller
The run is removed and trigger() returns it with state FAILED
The exception is swallowed and the run is retried on the calling thread

questions.prompt: What does activeCount() report at a given moment?
choices: Only builds currently executing on a worker thread
Builds that have finished but not yet been cleaned up
Builds that are queued or running, since entries are removed only after execution completes
The number of builds ever triggered
